claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is produced by conventional gas atomization.
Gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder typically has compositional inhomogeneities.
AlCrFeNiSi has a high risk of segregation when conventionally processed.
Preheating the powder bed or substrate during laser powder bed fusion reduces the thermal gradient between the melt pool and surrounding material.
The reduced thermal gradient slows the cooling rate.
Slower cooling enhances diffusion during solidification.
Enhanced diffusion promotes compositional homogenization in AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating AlCrFeNiSi during laser powder bed fusion reduces compositional segregation.
Preheating AlCrFeNiSi during laser powder bed fusion lowers residual thermal stress.
Preheating AlCrFeNiSi during laser powder bed fusion reduces process-induced defect density.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi develops a more uniform solid-solution microstructure.
A more uniform microstructure, reduced residual stress, and fewer defects improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than AlCrFeNiSi made by laser powder bed fusion without preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater room-temperature tensile strength than AlCrFeNiSi made by laser powder bed fusion without preheating.
Laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without preheating typically produces elevated segregation, residual stress, and rapid-cooling-related defects.
The hypothesized benefits apply over a preheat-temperature range of 400–600 °C under otherwise similar laser powder bed fusion conditions.
Preheating may cause adverse grain coarsening.
